papers.title: SSAlign: Fast and Sensitive Protein Structure Search at Scale
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Predicted protein structure resources now contain hundreds of millions of models, turning structural comparison from a pairwise alignment task into a database-scale retrieval problem. Exhaustive structural aligners are computationally impractical at this scale, whereas fast structural-alphabet searches may discard remote or low-complexity homologs during prefiltering. Database-scale search therefore requires methods that combine rapid retrieval with sensitivity to global structural similarity. Results We present SSAlign, a protein structure search method that integrates SaProt sequence-structure embeddings, entropy-reduced dense retrieval, an SS-score predictor and two-stage alignment refinement. In benchmarks on the Swiss-Prot, SCOPe40 and AFDB50 datasets, SSAlign showed competitive alignment quality and returned more TM-align-supported hits than Foldseek in recall-oriented evaluations. On AFDB50, 1,000 queries against 53.7 million structures completed in 3,150 s on CPUs and 2,290 s with GPU prefiltering, corresponding to 103-fold and 142-fold speedups over Foldseek, respectively. On SCOPe40, SSAlign increased the area under the curve (AUC) by 20.2% at family level and 33.3% at superfamily level. In simple-fold antimicrobial peptide case studies, SSAlign retrieved candidates that were not returned by Foldseek under the tested settings, indicating its utility as a fast candidate-generation tool for proteome-scale structural search. Availability and Implementation The source code for SSAlign is publicly available at https://github.com/ISYSLAB-HUST/SSAlign . The software version and test data used in this study are archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23432919 . Datasets and prebuilt indices can be downloaded from http://bioinfo.isyslab.info/ssalign/download/section/ssalign/

papers.title: Multi-View State-Space Modeling for Zero-Shot circRNA-miRNA Interaction Prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation CircRNA-miRNA interactions (CMIs) play regulatory roles in human diseases and provide clues for therapeutic target discovery. However, most existing prediction methods rely on circRNA-miRNA pairs and overlook disease-level regulatory contexts, which limits their ability to characterize cross-pathway dependencies in zero-shot inference. Results We propose MV-S 2 M, a multi-view state-space modeling framework that integrates molecular attributes to enhance relational reasoning, enabling zero-shot CMI prediction. Specifically, MV-S 2 M performs structure-aware diffusion to enrich molecular priors and constructs disease-mediated semantic subgraphs. It then incorporates state-space modeling to capture long-range dependencies and view-specific regulatory patterns. The learned multi-view representations are fused through a linear projection and fed into an MLP for CMI prediction. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that MV-S 2 M achieves state-of-the-art performance under both zero-shot and conventional settings. Cold-start evaluations reveal distinct generalization behavior across different unseen-entity settings. Case studies illustrate the contribution of meta-path-guided semantic subgraphs to CMI prediction. Availability and implementation The code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/591286260/MV and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22858403

papers.title: GBZ-base and GAF-base: Indexed pangenome file formats
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Existing pangenome file formats are designed for batch processing. Graphs must be loaded into memory, and alignment files must be read sequentially. Indexed file formats that can be used directly from disk would be more appropriate for interactive applications. Results We propose GBZ-base and GAF-base — SQLite-backed file formats comparable to GBZ and GAF. GBZ-base supports efficient extraction of local subgraphs, and GAF-base lets us extract all alignments to the subgraph. Additionally, GAF-base is smaller than any other file format for sequence-to-graph alignments. Availability and implementation From https://github.com/jltsiren/gbz-base and https://crates.io/crates/gbz-base under the MIT license

papers.title: Ernie-Switcher: RNA foundation model-guided design of programmable RNA devices in a navigable landscape
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Recent advances in biological foundation models have enabled new opportunities for data-driven molecular engineering. However, designing programmable RNA devices remains challenging because of the vast, nonlinear sequence-structure-function landscape. Here, we present Ernie-Switcher, a deep learning framework built upon the RNA foundation model (RNAErnie), comprising three coupled components: (i) integration of RNAErnie-derived sequence-phenotype representations for realistic design generation and filtering; (ii) characterization of RNA landscape navigability as a theoretical basis for sequence optimization; and (iii) incorporation of biophysical constraints to maintain optimization trajectories within biologically plausible bounds. Results We validated Ernie-Switcher using RNA toehold switches. Theoretically, the observed lower bound on threshold navigability (86.4%) of the RNA landscape supports the theoretical feasibility of RNA switch sequence optimization. Experimentally, the optimized toehold switches achieved ON/OFF expression ratios of up to 35-fold in Escherichia coli . Collectively, RNAErnie-guided sequence optimization provides a scalable strategy for engineering high-performance RNA devices. To facilitate broad adoption, we deployed Ernie-Switcher as a freely accessible web platform. Availability The Python code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/zhutiblah/Ernie-Switcher and are archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21859277 . The RNA toehold switch design platform is available at https://ernie-switcher.bioinformatics-syn.org/

all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Predicted protein structure resources now contain hundreds of millions of models, turning structural comparison from a pairwise alignment task into a database-scale retrieval problem. Exhaustive structural aligners are computationally impractical at this scale, whereas fast structural-alphabet searches may discard remote or low-complexity homologs during prefiltering. Database-scale search therefore requires methods that combine rapid retrieval with sensitivity to global structural similarity. Results We present SSAlign, a protein structure search method that integrates SaProt sequence-structure embeddings, entropy-reduced dense retrieval, an SS-score predictor and two-stage alignment refinement. all_papers.title: Multi-View State-Space Modeling for Zero-Shot circRNA-miRNA Interaction Prediction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation CircRNA-miRNA interactions (CMIs) play regulatory roles in human diseases and provide clues for therapeutic target discovery. However, most existing prediction methods rely on circRNA-miRNA pairs and overlook disease-level regulatory contexts, which limits their ability to characterize cross-pathway dependencies in zero-shot inference. Results We propose MV-S 2 M, a multi-view state-space modeling framework that integrates molecular attributes to enhance relational reasoning, enabling zero-shot CMI prediction. Specifically, MV-S 2 M performs structure-aware diffusion to enrich molecular priors and constructs disease-mediated semantic subgraphs. It then incorporates state-space modeling to capture long-range dependencies and view-specific regulatory patterns. The learned multi-view representations are fused through a linear projection and fed into an MLP for CMI prediction. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that MV-S 2 M achieves state-of-the-art performance under both zero-shot and conventional settings. Cold-start evaluations reveal distinct generalization behavior across different unseen-entity settings. Case studies illustrate the contribution of meta-path-guided semantic subgraphs to CMI prediction. Availability and implementation The code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/591286260/MV and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22858403

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: CircRNA-miRNA interactions (CMIs) play regulatory roles in human diseases and provide clues for therapeutic target discovery. However, most existing prediction methods rely on circRNA-miRNA pairs and overlook disease-level regulatory contexts, which limits their ability to characterize cross-pathway dependencies in zero-shot inference. Results We propose MV-S 2 M, a multi-view state-space modeling framework that integrates molecular attributes to enhance relational reasoning, enabling zero-shot CMI prediction. Specifically, MV-S 2 M performs structure-aware diffusion to enrich molecular priors and constructs disease-mediated semantic subgraphs. It then incorporates state-space modeling to capture long-range dependencies and view-specific regulatory patterns. The learned multi-view representations are fused through a linear projection and fed into an MLP for CMI prediction. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that MV-S 2 M achieves state-of-the-art performance under both zero-shot and conventional settings. Cold-start evaluations reveal distinct generalization behavior across different unseen-entity settings. Case studies illustrate the contribution of meta-path-guided semantic subgraphs to CMI prediction.

all_papers.title: Ernie-Switcher: RNA foundation model-guided design of programmable RNA devices in a navigable landscape
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Recent advances in biological foundation models have enabled new opportunities for data-driven molecular engineering. However, designing programmable RNA devices remains challenging because of the vast, nonlinear sequence-structure-function landscape. Here, we present Ernie-Switcher, a deep learning framework built upon the RNA foundation model (RNAErnie), comprising three coupled components: (i) integration of RNAErnie-derived sequence-phenotype representations for realistic design generation and filtering; (ii) characterization of RNA landscape navigability as a theoretical basis for sequence optimization; and (iii) incorporation of biophysical constraints to maintain optimization trajectories within biologically plausible bounds. Results We validated Ernie-Switcher using RNA toehold switches. Theoretically, the observed lower bound on threshold navigability (86.4%) of the RNA landscape supports the theoretical feasibility of RNA switch sequence optimization. Experimentally, the optimized toehold switches achieved ON/OFF expression ratios of up to 35-fold in Escherichia coli . Collectively, RNAErnie-guided sequence optimization provides a scalable strategy for engineering high-performance RNA devices. To facilitate broad adoption, we deployed Ernie-Switcher as a freely accessible web platform. Availability The Python code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/zhutiblah/Ernie-Switcher and are archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21859277 . The RNA toehold switch design platform is available at https://ernie-switcher.bioinformatics-syn.org/

all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Existing pangenome file formats are designed for batch processing. Graphs must be loaded into memory, and alignment files must be read sequentially.
